title: Finite affine enlargement of a quasi-compact pullback open
statement: Let $a:X\to A$ and $b:B\to A$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $A$ and $B$ affine. Suppose that every quasi-compact open subscheme of $X$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Quasi-compact means that every open covering admits a finite subcover. Put $Z=X\times_A B$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $p:Z\to X$. For every quasi-compact open subscheme $L\subseteq Z$, there exist $n\geq0$ and affine opens $W_1,\ldots,W_n\subseteq X$ such that $W=\bigcup_{j=1}^nW_j$ is quasi-compact and $p(|L|)\subseteq W$. The induced morphism $L\to W\times_A B$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $W\times_A B$ and $L$ are quasi-affine schemes. The morphism $W\times_A B\to B$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $a$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], the affine opens $V$ of $X$ cover $X$. Their inverse images under $p$ restrict to an open cover of $L$, since scheme morphisms are continuous. Quasi-compactness of $L$ gives finitely many such opens $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ with $p(|L|)\subseteq W=\bigcup_jW_j$. Each $W_j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For any open cover of $W$, restrict it to each $W_j$ and take a finite subcover there; the union of these finitely many finite subcovers covers $W$. Thus $W$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$, and the hypothesis makes $W$ quasi-affine. If $L$ is empty take $n=0$ and $W=\varnothing$.

source.place: lemma-ind-quasi-affine-composition, finite affine enlargement of the quasi-compact image; expanded open-cover argument

proof.text: Put $T=W\times_A B$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $T$ with $W\times_X Z$: a map to either side is a pair of maps to $W$ and $B$ whose composites to $A$ agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $T\to Z$ is an open immersion with image $p^{-1}(W)$. Indeed, after restriction to the open $W$, maps to $X$ factor uniquely and their structure sheaves restrict. Since $|L|\subseteq p^{-1}(W)$, $L$ is an open subset of $T$ and $\mathcal O_T|_L=\mathcal O_Z|_L=\mathcal O_L$. This is exactly the induced open immersion $L\to T$ by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: lemma-base-change-immersion (Tag 01JY), and the definition of an open subscheme

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-quasi-affine-target-locality] to $W\to A$ with the singleton affine cover $\{A\}$. Its inverse image is the quasi-affine scheme $W$ from step 1, so $W\to A$ is quasi-affine. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-base-change] along $b:B\to A$: the resulting morphism $T\to B$ is quasi-affine. Its inverse image of the affine open $B$ is $T$ itself, so $T$ is quasi-affine by [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism].

Choose an open embedding of the quasi-affine scheme $T$ into an affine scheme $H$. Under step 2, $L$ is an open subscheme of $T$, hence an open subscheme of $H$: its underlying subset is open, and restricting $\mathcal O_H$ first to $T$ and then to $L$ gives $\mathcal O_L$. Its given quasi-compactness makes this a quasi-compact open subscheme of $H$. Thus $L$ is quasi-affine. Together with steps 1–3 this proves every assertion.

lean.statement: theorem qc_open_pullback_quasi_affine_enlargement {X A B : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ A) (b : B ⟶ A) [IsAffine A] [IsAffine B] (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → U.toScheme.IsQuasiAffine) (L : (pullback a b).Opens) (hL : IsCompact (L : Set (pullback a b : Scheme.{u}))) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (Wj : Fin n → X.Opens) (W : X.Opens), (∀ j : Fin n, IsAffineOpen (Wj j)) ∧ W = iSup Wj ∧ IsCompact (W : Set X) ∧ Set.MapsTo (pullback.fst a b) (L : Set (pullback a b : Scheme.{u})) (W : Set X) ∧ (pullback (W.ι ≫ a) b).IsQuasiAffine ∧ L.toScheme.IsQuasiAffine ∧ IsQuasiAffineHom (pullback.snd (W.ι ≫ a) b) ∧ ∃ i : L.toScheme ⟶ pullback (W.ι ≫ a) b, IsOpenImmersion i ∧ i ≫ pullback.fst (W.ι ≫ a) b ≫ W.ι = L.ι ≫ pullback.fst a b ∧ i ≫ pullback.snd (W.ι ≫ a) b = L.ι ≫ pullback.snd a b

reviewed_lean.note: All clauses match the node: affine A and B, hX for quasi-compact opens of X, quasi-compact L, finite affine Wj with n=0 allowed, W = iSup Wj compact, p(L) ⊆ W via MapsTo, both pullback and L quasi-affine, snd quasi-affine via IsQuasiAffineHom. The open immersion i is the induced map: the two projection equations fix it because W.ι is mono. No extra hypotheses or universe restriction; lean.statement matches the file verbatim.
